name: Sow Good Inc.
business_overview: Sow Good Inc. operates as a distributor of freeze-dried candy and snack products. The company markets its products through a distribution partner. It offers its products under the Sow Good brand name. The company was formerly known as Black Ridge Oil & Gas, Inc. and changed its name to Sow Good Inc. in January 2021. Sow Good Inc. was founded in 2010 and is based in Irving, Texas.

classification_meta.logic_summary: Sow Good Inc. distributes freeze-dried candy and snack products under its own brand through distribution partners.

narrative.text:
**Business & market dynamics:** The legacy freeze-dried snack business has stalled, prompting an all-stock pivot into the Tanzanian Nachu Graphite Project to target the EV battery supply chain. This sudden entry into critical minerals introduces significant exposure to commodity-cycle volatility and geopolitical risks in a frontier mining jurisdiction. Market sentiment is deeply skeptical: short interest recently surged, and the sole analyst rating remains “Sell,” reflecting widespread doubt that the consumer-focused firm can credibly operate in extractive industries.

**Management strategy and execution:** Leadership radically recast the company through a dilutive, all-stock acquisition that effectively transfers majority ownership to the graphite asset’s sellers. A non-convertible credit facility was also secured. These moves are viewed as a high-stakes gamble well outside management’s historical expertise. The sharp rise in short positions and the negative analyst call underscore severe credibility questions about the team’s ability to execute an overseas mining build-out while managing a deteriorating legacy business.

# From Candy to Critical Minerals: Sow Good's $107M Graphite Gamble

IRVING, Texas – April 21, 2026 – In one of the most unconventional corporate pivots in recent memory, Sow Good Inc. (Nasdaq: SOWG), a company known for its trendy freeze-dried candies and snacks, has announced it is entering the high-stakes world of international mining. The company has agreed to acquire the Nachu Graphite Project in Tanzania in an all-stock deal valued at approximately US$107 million, a move it says will transform the small consumer goods firm into a key developer of critical minerals for the electric vehicle (EV) battery supply chain.
